Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline can identify every affected member and the card charged, so any settlement should deliver payments automatically rather than require claims. We propose a $40 million class fund, with fees and expenses paid separately and subject to court approval. Any reduction in the approved fee should benefit the class, not return to Brightline. We are open to discussing the amounts, but meaningful direct relief and these structural protections are important.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that identifiable members should receive payments automatically, and that any fee reduction should benefit the class. Your proposal would require a $48 million total outlay, which Brightline cannot accept. We offer a $30 million class fund plus up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing commitment.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline's agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. Those terms address important approval concerns. Given $64 million in disputed charges, we propose a $35 million class fund and $6.5 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses, with the same structural terms. The increase is directed principally toward affected members.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close, but your proposed $41.5 million total exceeds Brightline's settlement authority. We can offer a $33.5 million class fund and $6.5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, for a $40 million maximum total outlay. Payments would be automatic, and any fees not awarded would go to the class. We would not seek a clear-sailing provision.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $33.5 million class fund with automatic payments, plus up to $6.5 million in separately paid fees and expenses subject to court approval, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class. We will present the settlement and the complete negotiation transcript to the court.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial, defensible class recovery and a fee request that does not depend on reducing class payments. Automatic distribution is feasible because Brightline has the necessary records. Avoid a fee reversion or other terms that could create a conflict between counsel and the class.

The proposed $48 million total exceeds Brightline’s $40 million authorization. An automatic-distribution proposal with no fee reversion should improve approval prospects while leaving room to negotiate within the cap.

The $30 million automatic-distribution offer is substantial given trial and certification risks, but there is room to seek more direct class relief. Preserve the agreed distribution and fee-reduction protections; make a moderate counteroffer without tying class recovery to fees.

The latest proposal exceeds Brightline's $40 million total-outlay authority by $1.5 million. Counter at the authorized ceiling while preserving automatic distribution and the approval-friendly fee provisions.

The $33.5 million automatic class fund exceeds the $27.5 million undiscounted trial-value estimate and avoids certification risk and delay. The separately paid $6.5 million fee remains subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class. The terms are fair to the class and appropriate to accept.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this declaration in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The parties negotiated over three rounds. Our opening proposal sought a $40 million class fund and $8 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. Brightline countered with a $30 million fund and $6 million in fees and expenses. We proposed a $35 million fund and $6.5 million in fees and expenses; Brightline then offered the accepted terms: a $33.5 million class fund and up to $6.5 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. Throughout the negotiations, both sides agreed that identified members would receive payments automatically and that any fees not awarded would go to the class rather than Brightline. The settlement contains no clear-sailing provision. Fees were discussed alongside class relief from the first round, not only after class relief was agreed. The complete negotiation transcript will be filed for the Court’s review.
